page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the n2 family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage options.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the instance delivers modest compute performance. Stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests place the server in the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores are categorized as weak, with software compilation and ray tracing workloads also falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks register in the weak category, although the Passmark memory score achieves an average rating. Single-threaded gzip compression performs at an average level, whereas multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and image processing workloads show poor performance, landing in the bottom 10%.

The primary tradeoff of the n2-highmem-4 is its low compute density relative to its memory capacity, making it less suitable for CPU-bound tasks. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance provides a cost-effective entry point for memory-intensive workloads that do not require heavy parallel processing. It is best suited for small-scale databases, caching layers, memory-bound data processing, and general-purpose workloads requiring a larger memory footprint than standard instances.
